sections.body: The AI Accountant covers ten areas where artificial intelligence is changing accounting and finance, from the monthly close to the governance of the models themselves. In practice, AI now reads invoices, receipts, contracts and bank statements, matches transactions across ledgers, flags unusual entries, and drafts first versions of reports and reconciliations. Forecasting systems combine historical actuals with external signals to produce rolling cash and revenue projections, while tax tools sort transactions by jurisdiction and highlight rules that may apply. Audit and fraud work uses continuous sampling, pattern detection and link analysis to find outliers, duplicates and suspicious relationships in large data sets. Treasury, sustainability and digital asset teams use AI to reconcile bank positions, aggregate emissions data and track wallet activity. Governance work monitors model inputs, outputs, access and documentation so that the numbers can be explained and defended.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is furthest along in high volume, repetitive tasks such as document extraction, transaction matching, anomaly detection and basic forecasting. These tasks are largely solved in narrow settings, but they still depend on clean data, stable formats and human review for exceptions. Complex judgment remains hard, including materiality decisions, uncertain tax positions, audit opinions, fraud intent and the valuation of illiquid digital assets. Sustainability reporting and carbon accounting are especially unsettled because standards vary, data is estimated and assurance practices are still forming. Model governance is also incomplete, since many finance teams can deploy a tool faster than they can document its limits, test its bias or trace its output. The site tracks 222 compliance and regulation pages, a sign of how much of the real work sits in controls, evidence and regulatory expectations rather than in the model alone.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the money and the controls around it. Financial Reporting and Synthesis and Forecasting and Planning cover the close, the narrative and the forward view, so a reader goes there for how numbers are assembled and projected. Tax and Jurisdictional Compliance and Continuous Audit and Assurance deal with rules, evidence and testing, while Fraud Detection and Forensics and Payables and Receivables focus on transaction level risks and the cash conversion cycle. Treasury and Liquidity, Sustainability and Carbon Accounting and Digital Asset Accounting handle specialized balances and disclosures, from bank positions to emissions to tokens. Governance, Risk and Financial Data Security sits above them all, covering model oversight, access controls, data lineage and the security of the financial data supply chain. Read together, these pages show how AI moves from a helper in one workflow to a system that needs its own controls, owners and audit trail.
